review_workflow.how_to_use: Read the Priority column, set Status to approved or rejected in data/signals/suggestions.json, rebuild. Nothing in this build was implemented beyond the suggestions marked 'implemented' - i.e. the review step is real, not decorative.

meta.impact_scale: H = changes whether a decision can be made at all; M = changes decision quality or cost; L = convenience/clarity.
meta.path_note: The Recommended Path field is the ordering this session would execute in. It is a proposal for the reviewer to accept or edit, not a change already made.

suggestions.title: Stand up a price-history ingest before any modelling work
suggestions.problem: The repo has no market data. Without open/close snapshots per game per market, there is no target variable, no CLV, no backtest, and no line to originate against. Every other strategy page is architecture without a test.
suggestions.proposal: Add /data/inbox/lines/YYYY-MM-DD/{open,mid,close}.csv plus a normaliser that appends to an immutable store, keyed by game_id + market + line + timestamp + book. Snapshot even when a vendor trial is only 2 weeks long - it compounds.
suggestions.risk: Vendor terms may forbid the storage we need; scraping accounts get limited.

suggestions.title: Make the weekly injury report an append-only snapshot series
suggestions.problem: The official page serves one week at a time. If we only ever read 'current', we can never backtest availability impact - and history cannot be recovered later.
suggestions.proposal: Capture every report into /data/snapshots/injuries/2026-W10-{date}.json (the Week 10 file in this build is the first). Fetch Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and post-lock, because the *sequence* of designations is the signal, not the final state. Never overwrite a snapshot.
suggestions.risk: Low. Storage is trivial. Main risk is treating a mid-week snapshot as final.
suggestions.recommended_path: Phase 0, second item. First snapshot already captured by this session.

suggestions.title: Add a transactions feed (IR, elevations, waivers) as a first-class source
suggestions.problem: Verified in the Week 10 capture: a quarterback placed on injured reserve, and a mid-season trade, both appear in the league's news column but not as availability rows. A report-only pipeline is structurally blind to exactly the changes that redefine a team's depth for weeks.
suggestions.proposal: Daily transactions snapshot joined to the roster. Emit an alert whenever the transactions feed and the injury report disagree (e.g. a player IR'd but still carrying a game status, or a traded player still listed by his old club).
suggestions.risk: Cadence varies by club; missing rows look like 'nothing happened'.

suggestions.title: Score availability predictions against the actual game-day inactives, not against the Friday report
suggestions.problem: The report is an input; the inactive list is the truth of who played. Scoring a model against its own input is circular and flatters the model.
suggestions.proposal: After each game, store the inactive list plus verified snap counts, and make 'predicted availability vs actual participation' a tracked metric with its own accuracy line on the dashboard.
suggestions.risk: Snap data may be licensed (Q-ROSTER-03); box-score aggregates are a fallback.

suggestions.title: Replace 'players out' counts with a position-weighted replacement ladder
suggestions.problem: Counting absences treats a starting centre and a slot cornerback as the same loss. The count-based signal in the current snapshot (e.g. IND 6 out, MIN 5 out) is honest but crude and cannot be compared across teams without weighting.
suggestions.proposal: value_gap = sum over positions of (starter_quality - expected_replacement_quality) x snaps. Coefficients estimated by regression once SG-04 data exists; until then the ladder is marked 'estimated, unvalidated' wherever it appears.
suggestions.risk: First-draft coefficients are priors dressed as numbers if the estimation step is skipped.

suggestions.title: Publish CLV as the headline leaderboard metric and log it from day one
suggestions.problem: A leaderboard ranked on PnL rewards variance for the first few hundred bets, which is the opposite of the brief's 'selectively skill based'.
suggestions.proposal: Every bet row stores: price taken, closing price of the anchor, cents beaten, timestamp. Leaderboard score = luck-adjusted (see SG-07), PnL shown greyed with a 'not yet significant' marker until the sample gate passes.
suggestions.risk: CLV is gameable if the anchor book is soft; mitigate by fixing the anchor before the season (Q-MKT-02).

suggestions.title: Score strategies on luck-adjusted growth, not on win rate
suggestions.problem: Win rate and ROI both contain run luck. A skill-based leaderboard needs a metric whose noise is quantified, so a lucky run cannot outrank a better process.
suggestions.proposal: Rank on t-statistic of CLV-per-bet and on log-growth after fractional Kelly, both computed on a rolling window; require the sample gate; break ties by how stable the metric is across sub-periods, not by recent hot streaks.
suggestions.risk: Sample-size inflation: a strategy that bets everything more often reaches significance first. Fix with a minimum-signal-quality floor per bet.

suggestions.title: Keep a decision journal that records every failed variant
suggestions.problem: Multiple testing is the mechanism by which 'no luck' systems still pick winners by luck. If 40 model variants are tried and only the survivor is reported, the survivor's statistics are meaningless.
suggestions.proposal: Append-only journal: variant id, hypothesis, config hash, data hash, result - including the 39 that failed. Gates read the count of trials from it and apply the correction automatically.
suggestions.risk: None, other than it slows down quiet retuning (that is the point).
suggestions.recommended_path: Phase 1. The journal file is created by this build as a stub.

suggestions.title: Encode the validation gates as executable code, not as documentation
suggestions.problem: Gates described in prose are advisory. A gate that is a function returning pass/fail cannot be argued with under pressure, which is exactly when gates get bent.
suggestions.proposal: /tools/gates.py implements each gate in data/signals/gates.json; the builder refuses to promote a strategy whose gate list is not all-pass; the site renders pass/fail from the run artefact, never from a hand-edit.
suggestions.risk: Blank thresholds mean the code cannot run yet - each blank is itself a flagged question.
suggestions.owner_needed: reviewer must set 5 numeric thresholds (see flagged F-05)

suggestions.title: Timestamp audit: prove each input existed before the lock
suggestions.problem: Injury reports, news and line snapshots all have publication times, and look-ahead leakage in betting models comes almost entirely from using a fact that was published after the price moved.
suggestions.proposal: Every field in every dataset carries fetched_at and published_at. The backtest engine can only read a field whose published_at precedes the bet timestamp; violation is a hard error, not a warning.
suggestions.risk: Some sources publish no explicit timestamp; those fields must be marked low-confidence or excluded.

suggestions.title: Measure parlay leg correlation empirically and refuse to price unmeasured pairs
suggestions.problem: Correlation is the difference between a fair parlay and one that quietly donates margin. The brief asks for correlation values to be determined; today no measurement exists in this repo, and inventing one would be the exact failure mode the project is meant to avoid.
suggestions.proposal: Compute joint settlement rates for each leg-pair from the bet ledger with bootstrap confidence intervals. Until n >= the minimum, publish the pair with a blank value and a 'not priced' status.
suggestions.risk: Rare leg-pairs may never accumulate enough observations; accept and say so.

suggestions.title: Add weather, roof status and travel/rest to the feature set
suggestions.problem: Totals are sensitive to wind and to a roof being closed; the Week 10 slate also contains a 9:30 AM ET international game in Munich, where rest and travel are part of the price and not in any injury column.
suggestions.proposal: Ingest a public meteorological forecast per venue (an official government source, timestamped) plus the league's confirmed roof/travel status; store as separate dated snapshots so the pre-game version is what the model sees.
suggestions.risk: Forecast revision means a backtest using today's archive of the forecast differs from what was knowable at the time - must use forecast archives, not re-forecasts.

suggestions.title: Treat line-shopping as a strategy, ranked on the same board as models
suggestions.problem: Getting the best available price is a guaranteed, measurable edge that most of a research budget should go to before any model is built, yet it usually sits outside the leaderboard and so competes for nothing.
suggestions.proposal: Model a 'shopping only' entry (S-12) on the leaderboard with the same gates. If no model can beat it after costs, the honest conclusion is that we do not yet have a signal.
suggestions.risk: Rewards limit-capped micro-edges that do not survive stake size.

suggestions.title: Publish a per-source freshness and coverage panel on the dashboard
suggestions.problem: A reviewer must be able to see at a glance which numbers are live, which are 3 days old, and which are blank because a source could not be read. Silent staleness in a wagering system is a decision hazard.
suggestions.proposal: Implemented in this build: every table header carries as_of and a TTL, and the dashboard banner shows worst-case staleness. Next step is a per-source coverage bar (rows expected vs rows captured).
suggestions.risk: None.

suggestions.title: Add a diff view between consecutive snapshots
suggestions.problem: The actionable event is a *change* (a starter moving from Questionable to Out after the line was set), not a state. Without a diff, that event is invisible unless a human reads two tables.
suggestions.proposal: When two snapshots of the same week exist, render added/removed/changed rows with the timestamp of each change and the price available at that moment.
suggestions.risk: Needs at least two snapshots, so it starts empty.
suggestions.recommended_path: Phase 1, once the second snapshot exists.

suggestions.title: Give the Flagged for Review page a one-line action control
suggestions.problem: A flagged row that nobody can disposition becomes permanent noise; the brief's workflow is review-then-choose, so review has to be cheap.
suggestions.proposal: Each flagged row gets three buttons that open a pre-filled PR comment (resolve with value / accept blank / suppress with reason), so dispositioning the board is minutes, not an editing session.
suggestions.risk: None.

suggestions.title: Descope player-prop combos until snap-level data is licensed
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for prop bet combos. Props are decided by usage, and usage data is the one input here with no confirmed availability. Modelling props from season priors would produce confident, wrong numbers on the thinnest market.
suggestions.proposal: Keep prop strategies in the catalogue at status 'research-only, blocked' with the blocking question named, and make the site say plainly that no prop line is originated yet.
suggestions.risk: Reviewer may consider this too cautious; it is still the alternative to shipping fabricated edges.

suggestions.title: Add an adversarial red-team pass before any strategy reaches live money
suggestions.problem: A gate suite proves a strategy survived the tests we thought of. Strategies usually die from a case we did not think of (a voided leg, a limit change, a rule quirk, a Monday refiling).
suggestions.proposal: For each candidate strategy, require a written 'how this loses' section plus one simulated adverse week; the site renders it next to the edge claim so optimism cannot travel alone.
suggestions.risk: Checklist theatre if not read by a second party.

suggestions.title: Separate 'the number is wrong' from 'the number is missing' in the flag taxonomy
suggestions.problem: Two different failures need two different owners: a wrong value is a data-quality bug, a missing value is a procurement gap. Merged into one list, the procurement gaps never get closed.
suggestions.proposal: Add a flag type field (value-conflict / not-obtainable / source-changed / semantic-ambiguity) and route each type to a different action. Implemented in this build's flag schema.
suggestions.risk: None.

suggestions.title: Cap strategy count rather than adding more strategies
suggestions.problem: This build ships 16 candidate strategies. Every additional variant raises the bar the survivors must clear (multiple-testing correction), so a longer catalogue can make it *harder* for any strategy to be provably real.
suggestions.proposal: Freeze the catalogue at the current list, promote at most 3 to development, and require a slot to be retired before a new one is added.
suggestions.risk: May leave a genuinely good idea waiting.

suggestions.title: Add an 'information we do not have' register next to every strategy
suggestions.problem: The brief asks suggestions to be made to discover missing information. A strategy page that lists only its design hides the reason it cannot run.
suggestions.proposal: Implemented in this build: each strategy carries blocked_on listing the missing input and a link to the exact question that resolves it.
suggestions.risk: None.

recommended_path_sequence.exit_criteria: Price snapshots and two or more dated availability snapshots for the same week exist in the repo, each row source-linked.
CLV and availability-accuracy reportable for real events; failed variants logged.

recommended_path_sequence.phase: Phase 2 - Models and gates as code
recommended_path_sequence.exit_criteria: gates.py runs in CI; every strategy has a pass/fail record with a config hash.
Parlays priced on measured correlation only; exposure caps enforced.

recommended_path_sequence.phase: Phase 4 - Capital, if and only if gates pass
recommended_path_sequence.exit_criteria: Reviewer-approved budget, legal confirmation, one strategy at a time, kill switch armed.
